reflection.text:
Unblinded truth is mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II-alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor (PMID 27834128, PMID 22140093), scored as DNA replication; I concluded Actin disruptors at p=0.35 and was wrong. What I did detect correctly was the nuclear replication-stress signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0 at 0.3 uM rising to +61.1 at 1 uM and +35.0 at 3 uM with nuc_solidity z=-29.8 and microscopist-noted lower density, which fits replication-fork arrest at topoisomerase II cleavage sites (PMID 9153414) rather than a primary cytoskeletal lesion.

I was misled by actin texture/brightness (act_glcm_contrast up to +26.1, act_std +24.9) and visual actin rims at 1-3 uM (e5-e7), which I promoted to 0.55 in step 15 despite the atlas voting 0/10 for Actin in e8 (5/10 Microtubule destabilizers) and e20 (7/10 Microtubule stabilizers). The dose-response comparison already warned me: cell_roundness rho=+1.00 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 were monotonic while act_std rho=-0.20, act_glcm_contrast rho=-0.40 and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 peaked at 1-3 uM and collapsed at 10 uM, and the 10 uM well had only 6 cells with extreme z-scores (roundness +39.4), making the high-dose rounding unreliable.

The acquisition choice compounded this: I sampled only single replicates at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM in the toxic/arrested range and never acquired the requested 0.1 uM onset test to order actin-first versus tubulin/nuclear-first, left DNA damage and DNA replication at 0.03-0.10, and ran no DNA-specific readout. I treated multinucleation and rounding as actin-driven cytokinesis failure without testing that topo inhibition/DNA damage itself produces G2 enlargement, mitotic rounding and secondary actin remodeling.

what_was_wrong: Interpreted act_glcm_contrast, act_std and visual rims at 0.3-3 uM as primary actin disruption despite negative/monotonic-failing dose responses (rho -0.20 to -0.40)
Overrode two atlas comparisons with 0 Actin neighbors (5/10 destabilizer then 7/10 stabilizer) in favor of visual e7 which listed Aurora equally
Kept DNA replication/DNA damage at 0.03-0.10 despite massive large-nucleus signal and did not consider secondary cytoskeletal remodeling from replication stress

## Reflection

Unblinded truth is mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II-alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor (PMID 27834128, PMID 22140093), scored as DNA replication; I concluded Actin disruptors at p=0.35 and was wrong. What I did detect correctly was the nuclear replication-stress signal: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0 at 0.3 uM rising to +61.1 at 1 uM and +35.0 at 3 uM with nuc_solidity z=-29.8 and microscopist-noted lower density, which fits replication-fork arrest at topoisomerase II cleavage sites (PMID 9153414) rather than a primary cytoskeletal lesion.

I treated multinucleation and rounding as actin-driven cytokinesis failure without testing that topo inhibition/DNA damage itself produces G2 enlargement, mitotic rounding and secondary actin remodeling.

What was right:
- Captured very large nuclear phenotype (frac_large_nucleus up to +61.1, nuc_solidity -29.8, lower density) consistent with topo-II replication arrest
- Noted monotonic tubulin contrast/rounding versus non-monotonic actin and flagged Microtubule destabilizer/Aurora alternatives, lowering Actin 0.55 to 0.35
- Recognized single-replicate design and n=6 at 10 uM made confidence overprecise

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted act_glcm_contrast, act_std and visual rims at 0.3-3 uM as primary actin disruption despite negative/monotonic-failing dose responses (rho -0.20 to -0.40)
- Overrode two atlas comparisons with 0 Actin neighbors (5/10 destabilizer then 7/10 stabilizer) in favor of visual e7 which listed Aurora equally
- Kept DNA replication/DNA damage at 0.03-0.10 despite massive large-nucleus signal and did not consider secondary cytoskeletal remodeling from replication stress
- Stayed in high-dose toxic range with single replicates and did not acquire 0.1 uM onset or DNA readouts to test primary versus secondary

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose titration 0.03-1 uM in triplicate with EdU pulse, gamma-H2AX, DNA-content flow and phospho-H3 plus cytochalasin-D and vincristine controls to test whether loss of EdU / H2AX foci and large irregular nuclei precede actin texture and rounding, proving cytoskeletal changes are secondary to topoisomerase-II replication arrest.
